newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe rights group urges atrocities probe.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe rights group urges atrocities probe.

text.p: A Zimbabwe human rights workshop called on Tuesday for an independent inquiry into alleged atrocities committed by government troops when they crashed an armed rebellion in the country's southern provinces in the 1980s.

The official ZIANA news agency reported that some of the particpants, who declined to be identified, called on the government of President Robert Mugabe to organise a forum where the victims of the alleged atrocities could speak out.
"People are still harbouring ill feelings of what happened in that dark hour and a commission is required to redress the situation and work out reparations for the victims," a participant said.

Southern Zimbabwe, home to the minority Ndebele tribe of Vice-President Joshua Nkomo, erupted in armed rebellion against Mugabe's government in 1982. Ndebeles comprise about 25 percent of Zimbabwe's population of 10 million.
The civil strife ended in 1987 with the signing of a unity accord between Nkomo's then opposition PF-ZAPU party and the ruling ZANU-PF which saw Nkomo appointed vice-president.
But charges of brutal killings, torture and rape of innocent civilians by government troops and state-engineered disappearances have dogged Mugabe's government for the past 10 years.
Mugabe has over the years ignored calls for an independent probe into the allegations and for restitution to victims.
The workshop was held in the southwestern city of Bulawayo.
